messages:
keerthi: kicking off quick KV prefetch + quant bench. goal: measure hitrate vs token latency and paging for int8 vs fp16 across H100 (us-west1) and A100 (eu-west1) using seqlen mix [70%,25%,5%] for 8/64/512. harness: nightly-kv-bench v3.
bench-bot: artifacts will be uploaded here: https://internal.redwood/bench/artifacts/1702991234 (auto post when complete). queued runs: 8.
bench-bot: initial small summary (dry run):
``
variant gpu    seqlen_mix  hitrate p50_ms p95_ms paging_ops/s evict/s
fp16    H100   70/25/5     0.84    5.9   16.1   10            0.9
int8    H100   70/25/5     0.79    5.4   24.3   26            2.8
fp16    A100   70/25/5     0.81    7.2   19.8   16            1.6
int8    A100   70/25/5     0.76    6.8   31.0   40            4.1
```
keerthi: surprise: int8 wins median but tail explodes, consistent with extra paging and evictions.
maria: can we see per-seqlen hitrate? long requests likely killing int8.
bench-bot: uploaded per-seqlen CSV + eviction heatmap to artifacts. short summary: for seqlen=512 hitrate drops ~0.25 for int8 vs fp16.
jon: this suggests two levers: prefetch tuning and sequence-length based routing. also kernel selection hints might change int8 tail (kernel_pref=latency vs throughput).
sophie: suggestion: try prefetch_window {0,1,2} and prefetch_threshold {0.6,0.8} for int8 on both GPUs, keep fp16 baseline. also try kernel_policy=latency_prefer. small-batch cap change: batch_max_tokens 512 -> 1024 to see batching effect.
keerthi: agreed. schedule matrix: int8 x {prefetch 0,1,2} x {pref_thresh 0.6,0.8} x kernel_policy {auto,latency_prefer} x GPUs H100/A100. will capture hitrate per seqlen, p50/p95 token latency, paging_ops, evict_rate, gpu_mem_frag.
bench-bot: enqueued 24 jobs. est runtime ~4h per region. posting job ids as they start.
infra-bot: note: prefetch increases GPU memory pressure; cluster autoscaler may bump nodes. tracking mem_frag metric in prometheus.
maria: also add a small QA sample (500 prompts) for quant quality regression check. want to ensure no perf gain at cost of hallucination.
jon: +1 — add BLEU/ROUGE-ish and embedding-sim threshold checks.
sophie: while this runs, quick cost calc — int8 throughput improvement is ~1.5x on short seqs but paging IO for tails increases effective token cost by ~1.3x in our rough calc. sequence-based routing might be net positive.
bench-bot: job 1702991234-3 finished (H100, int8, prefetch=2, thresh=0.8, kernel=latency_prefer). artifacts: https://internal.redwood/bench/artifacts/1702991234/1702991234-3
bench-bot: diff vs int8 baseline (prefetch=0) on H100:
- hitrate overall +0.06
- seqlen512 hitrate +0.18
- p95 token -9.2ms
- paging_ops -42%
- evict_rate -55%
keerthi: nice. prefetch=2 with higher threshold really helps H100 int8 tail.
jon: any change in gpu_mem_frag?
bench-bot: mem_frag +3% on average, concurrency unchanged for our test load.
maria: QA eval on sample prompts shows negligible embedding drift (mean cosine 0.993) and answer pass rate 98/100. no glaring regressions.
sophie: A100 results for same config?
bench-bot: job 1702991234-7 finished (A100, int8, prefetch=2, thresh=0.8, kernel=latency_prefer). summary:
- seqlen512 hitrate +0.10
- p95 token -5.6ms
- paging_ops -28%
- evict_rate -35%
- mem_frag +4%
- QA pass 97/100, embedding cos 0.990
keerthi: so prefetch helps both GPUs, H100 sees larger tail improvement. A100 still worse than fp16 on tails for int8 but improved.
jon: next: run kernel_policy=throughput_prefer for int8+prefetch=2 to compare. sometimes different kernels manage memory movement better.
bench-bot: queued those jobs. also attaching raw CSVs for cost model.
sophie: routing thought: if we detect seqlen>256, route to fp16 in eu-west1 (A100) where fp16 tail is relatively better; keep medium/short on int8 in us-west1 H100 with prefetch=2. but need cost calc including cross-region egress and extra paging IO.
keerthi: good plan. infra: can you prototype a seqlen routing rule in dev canary? small percentage rollout.
infra-bot: will stand up rule in dev canary, need platform to expose rollout flag. ETA EOD tomorrow.
maria: I'll prepare a regression checklist + automated smoke evals to run as part of canary. will post PR for review.
jon: action items recap:
- bench-bot: finish kernel_policy matrix + attach CSVs and heatmaps
- infra: prototype seqlen routing in dev canary
- platform: cost delta per region + egress/paging IO cost estimate
- qa: run quant quality checks on 500-prompt set per job
bench-bot: remaining jobs done. final note: combined strategy (int8+prefetch on H100 for short/med; fp16 for long in eu) shows ~12% overall cost saving for our sample traffic mix and keeps p95 within SLA. details in artifacts.
keerthi: great. I'll draft rollout runbook and post here for review. thanks all. :thumbsup:
